_comment: The shapes an identifier takes, written once and read by both languages.
This file exists because redaction is about to run in two places: in the
browser, where it keeps the patient's name off the network entirely, and on
the server, which redacts again as a backstop. Two implementations of the
same rules is the one real risk in that design — a pattern fixed in Python
and not in JavaScript is a leak that every test still passes.
So neither language owns these. backend/redaction.py loads this file at
import and refuses to start without it; extension/privacy/redact.js fetches
it from the packaged extension and refuses to redact without it.
It lives under extension/ because a Chrome extension can only read files
inside its own directory, and the backend has no such restriction.
SYNTAX: every regex here must be valid in BOTH Python's re and JavaScript's
RegExp. That rules out named groups spelled differently, \Z, and inline
flags. Lookbehind is fine — Python has always had it and V8 has since
Chrome 62, well under the extension's minimum of 114.
TOKENS: `start` is the first counter value, and 1 versus 2 is not
arbitrary. [NRIC] and [PHONE] without a number are the patient's own, put
there by the dictionary pass; numbering the pattern pass from 2 keeps a
family member's NRIC from being handed back as the patient's on re-merge.
SHIELDS are the opposite of patterns: spans held aside so the passes cannot
touch them, and restored afterwards. They are here for the same reason the
patterns are — an over-redaction bug fixed in one language and not the other
costs the form a field, quietly, in only one of the two places redaction runs.

patterns.note: Singapore NRIC/FIN. A single optional space is tolerated either side of the digits, because a doctor typing from a card leaves them.
Singapore mobile or landline. The lookaround stops a longer digit run — an invoice number, a policy number's tail — being read as a phone.
No form asks for one, so it is only ever removed, never returned.

shields.name: institution
shields.note: An institution's name routinely contains somebody's surname — Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital. Pass 1 redacts each part of the patient's name, so a patient surnamed Tan turned that hospital into '[PATIENT] Tock Seng Hospital' and the claim lost the field asking which hospital. These spans are held aside for the length of the passes and put back after. A facility is not a patient.
